High-performance computing (HPC) refers to the practice of aggregating computing power to solve large
problems in science, engineering, or business. The adoption of HPC is gaining traction as enterprises
across key verticals are focusing on scaling up their infrastructure for cloud computing and edge
computing by integrating them with digital technologies such as AI, IoT, and big data analytics. HPC
enables the community of researchers, scientists, and engineers working in various fields to solve complex,
compute-intensive problems in a short period. Benefits associated with HPC are high network
performance, fast storage, and the ability to process large volumes of data. HPC also enables organizations
to develop new, innovative products and services to maintain a competitive edge.
HPC has gradually evolved over the decades and undergone various technological innovations and
advancements. In the early 1970s, the vector computing system concept was used with distributed
memory systems and had the processing capability of Megaflops/second (Mflops/s). In the early 1990s,
the Massively Parallel Processing (MPP) theory was used in large enterprises and SMEs, where systems
were equipped with “off-the-shelf components” and had a processing speed of up to multiple
Gigaflops/second (Gflops/s). In 2000, this speed increased to teraflops, and by 2008 the computational
speed reached petaflops. Since then, supercomputers have become billion times faster, and the HPC

sections.heading: Cyber security concerns
content: With the growing use of HPC systems, concerns regarding cyber security are also rising as several entities
access HPC systems, making data security a major concern. The nature of HPC exposes it to multiple

vulnerable to many security threats. Since clustered HPC systems are heterogeneous, they require multiple
management systems to operate. This slows down the implementation of security policies and security
management processes; as a result, vulnerabilities are not remediated. Thus, security concerns are
expected to restrain the growth of the HPC market.

capabilities, requires a large investment. For instance, an entry-level commercial cluster may require a
budget of anywhere between USD 10,000 and 25,000. The deployment of advanced systems with a large
number of nodes is more expensive.

sections.heading: (HPC)
content: HPC was a mature and conventional area of information technology. It was distinguished by a narrow
category of applications used by a fundamentally fixed set of industries, primarily using on-premise
systems. But over the last few years, all of that has started to change. New technologies, the cloud, and a
developing set of commercial use cases in the field of machine learning and data analytics have set in

or keep pace with their industry peers to survive. However, there is a scarcity of skills and available training
in HPC to prepare and expand the workforce for the HPC and Big Data research and development.
Limited budgets of SMEs
The potential users in many SMEs lack awareness about the benefits of HPC and do not have the budget to
set up such systems. SMEs in many developing countries are still skeptical about adopting HPC due to the
high investment costs involved. Many of them are unaware of HPC’s various advantages, such as high
performance and customizable delivery. However, cloud computing can boost the use of HPC among SMEs,
as it will considerably cut down the costs for them.
Challenges in cooling HPC systems
HPC systems have massive power and storage demands. As the power and storage demands of these HPC
deployments continue to grow, the air-cooling technology does not offer a viable solution. High-density
servers are required for HPC, which generate heat faster, resulting in high-temperature levels. Liquid
cooling is more suitable for high-density facilities as it is both cost- and energy-efficient. Liquid cooling
solutions are said to reduce cooling energy consumption by 40–50% and improve Power Usage
Effectiveness (PUE). This reduction in energy consumption leads to a reduction in carbon footprint, which is
both environmental and economical. These benefits provided by liquid cooling are expected to attract
widespread demand from HPC facilities.

sections.heading: and ensure resiliency
content: HPC systems are susceptible to soft errors in both logic circuits and memory subsystems and fail-stop
errors in the entire system. Scientific simulations that run on HPC devices use iterative logic to solve
complex problems, which require massive processing power. Such massive computing power requires
parallelism with at least 100,000 nodes to achieve sustained Petascale performance. However, systems
having 100,000 nodes and a large Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF) may encounter a failure every nine
hours on average. Even larger systems may encounter failures every hour. Designing a fault-tolerant
system is therefore challenging and requires multiple approaches at different levels of the software stack.
Advanced algorithms are needed to ensure proper process checkpointing at the lowest level (operating
system) as well as at the system level. The advanced distributed checkpointing framework may be needed
to design rollback recovery procedures at the parallel application level.

content: Over the past few decades, there has been an exponential increase in the volumes of structured and

sections.heading: NETWORKING DEVICES
content: HPC infrastructure requirements differ from organization to organization. Thus, a standard networking
infrastructure cannot be used. Depending upon the organization’s demand, the HPC infrastructure has to
be integrated with application-specific networking infrastructure to leverage the HPC capabilities.
Furthermore, traditional networks are highly static and associated with high operational overheads and
manual intervention. They act as a bottleneck in supporting varied HPC applications and are usually
configured to handle a specific application. Thus, organizations prefer highly scalable and easily
manageable network infrastructure. HPC networking devices cater to these requirements, enabling
organizations to use HPC solutions optimally. HPC networking devices include ethernet switches, ethernet
network interface cards, Local Area Network (LAN) interconnections, InfiniBand, adapters, and routers.
Among these, Ethernet and InfiniBand are gaining significant traction in the HPC market. Major vendors
offering networking devices include DDN, Dell, and Cisco.

systems are becoming complex featuring different heterogeneous hardware components to accommodate
different workloads, programmers need software development tools to ease application development and
aid with targeted performance tuning and optimization. A typical HPC software suite comprises a
comprehensive collection of highly tuned linear algebra subroutines designed to help extract maximum
performance from the HPC system with the least amount of effort. Companies such as Hewlett Packard

PROBLEMS
content: In parallel computing, multiple processing elements run simultaneously to solve complex problems. These
problems are divided into smaller problems, and a dedicated computing resource is assigned to solve
them. Parallel computing has gained popularity across various applications in the industrial sector. The use
of other computing techniques has physical constraints that prevent frequency scaling, thereby reducing
the system’s capability of operating at optimal computational speeds. Parallel computing has become the
dominant standard in computer architecture, as it is being increasingly used in modern multi-core
processors due to its less power consumption and heat generation features in data processing.
In parallel computing, a single computer is equipped with multiple processors to perform numerous
operations. The system may have a shared or distributed memory architecture that improves the system
performance in applications related to computer vision, such as fault detection. Parallel computing is also
being used in video and image processing, deep learning and machine learning, web services, natural
language processing, autonomous driving, medicine, drug discovery, and biotechnology.

sections.heading: BIT-LEVEL PARALLELISM
content: A bit-level parallelism is a form of parallel computing that increases the processor’s word size. A word is
defined as an entity that comprises computing bits. Increasing the word size reduces the number of
instructions the processor is required to execute to perform a process on variables whose sizes are more
than the length of the word. For example, a processor with a 32-bit word size can perform 4 independent 1-
byte additions simultaneously. If the processor size is 1 byte, it will perform 4 operations.

sections.heading: INSTRUCTION-LEVEL PARALLELISM
content: Instruction-level parallelism is an architecture in which multiple operations can be performed parallelly in a
particular process with a set of resources such as identifiers, address space, registers, state, and program
counters. Instruction-level parallelism refers to the compiler design techniques and processors designed to
execute operations such as memory load and store, integer addition, and float multiplication. These
techniques enhance the performance of processors. Examples of architectures that use instruction-level
parallelism are very long instruction words and superscalar computing architectures. The execution
hardware in a typical instruction-level parallelism processor is similar to that of a reduced instruction set
computer (RISC) machine. The difference between a machine with instruction-level parallelism and one
without is that there may be more hardware components present, such as a number of integer adders
rather than just one hardware component, and that the control will allow, and possibly arrange,
simultaneous access to whatever execution hardware is present.

sections.heading: TASK PARALLELISM
content: Task parallelism, also known as functional or control parallelism, uses algorithmic decomposition to break
down a massive task into several subtasks, which helps in multiplying computing resources. The key
advantage associated with this technique is multiple portions of the visualization task to be executed are
performed in parallel mode. The main disadvantage of this technique is that the number of independent
tasks that can be processed simultaneously, as well as the number of CPUs available to accomplish it,
limits the maximum amount of parallelism. In addition, it can be difficult to load-balance the tasks and,
therefore, can be challenging to take full advantage of the available resources. Task parallelism is used
effectively in the entertainment industry, where several frames in an animated production are rendered in
parallel. Specific hardware choices for improving the performance of task parallelism are dependent upon
the details of the required tasks.

content: Distributed computing is also called distributed processing. A distributed computer system consists of
multiple software components that are spread across various computers within the network but are
operated as a single system. The computers in a distributed system can be connected by a local network or
a wide area network. A distributed system can consist of many possible configurations, such as
mainframes, personal computers, workstations, and minicomputers. The goal of distributed computing is
to make a mesh of computer networks work as a single computer.
High-performance computing makes use of distributed computing facilities for solving problems that need
high computing power. Distributed computing in HPC connects multiple computer servers over a network
into a cluster to share data and coordinate data processing. Such a cluster is referred to as a “distributed
system.” Distributed computing offers advantages such as scalability, performance resilience, and cost-
effectiveness using low-cost, commodity hardware.

sections.heading: CLUSTER COMPUTING
content: Cluster computing refers to various computer systems connected across a network that perform like a
single entity. Each computer that is connected to the network is called a node. Cluster computing offers

integrity. The connected computers work in tandem to execute operations, thus creating the impression of
